When we visited their workshop, they only partially addressed the issue by removing some of the paint transfer and scratches. Since it was already around 11:30 PM, we were told to return the next day so the remaining repairs, including the dents on the rear bumper, could be completed.

The next day, the person identifying himself as Alam (who claimed to be the owner) was unwilling to send his staff to complete the promised repairs. Instead of resolving the issue professionally, he repeatedly raised his voice and argued, despite the fact that the accident was caused by their employee. He seemed more concerned about damage to the vehicle he had lent to Ashraf than about the damage caused to our car.

What made the situation even more concerning was that Ashraf was driving a vehicle without number plates and, according to what we were told, did not have a valid driving licence.

I ended up waiting for nearly three hours and repeatedly following up before any additional work was done. Even then, the repairs were not completed to the standard that had been promised, and I ultimately had to bear part of the loss myself.

I also have a written bill from the workshop stating “Ashraf ne dent kiya hai” and referencing the repair of the rear bumper, which acknowledges responsibility for the damage.

I would strongly advise customers to be cautious. If a business is not prepared to honor commitments made by its employees, it should not make promises to customers in the first place. Based on my experience, I would not recommend Car Fashion.
